Author: Baruch Spinoza
Title: Theological-Political Treatise
Core Question / Why Read: Why should prophets or scripture possess special authority?
Relationship to Your View: Very close on anti-anthropomorphism and critique of privileged revelation

Author: Kabir
Title: The Bijak of Kabir
Core Question / Why Read: Can religious identity and ritual obstruct encounter with reality?
Relationship to Your View: Close on anti-sectarianism and criticism of religious authority

Author: Baruch Spinoza
Title: Ethics
Core Question / Why Read: What does it mean for everything to exist in God/Nature?
Relationship to Your View: Very close metaphysically; rejects divine purposes modeled on human intention

Author: William C. Chittick
Title: Imaginal Worlds: Ibn al-Arabi and the Problem of Religious Diversity
Core Question / Why Read: How can one Reality disclose itself through diverse forms?
Relationship to Your View: Close on divine manifestation; differs on prophetic hierarchy

Author: Dara Shikoh
Title: The Mingling of the Two Oceans
Core Question / Why Read: Can different traditions articulate the same ultimate reality?
Relationship to Your View: Close on pluralism; retains Islamic revelation and prophecy

Author: John Hick
Title: An Interpretation of Religion
Core Question / Why Read: Are religions culturally conditioned responses to an ultimate Reality?
Relationship to Your View: Close on pluralism; less radical than your universal sacredness claim

Author: Simone de Beauvoir
Title: The Ethics of Ambiguity
Core Question / Why Read: How can we act ethically without absolute or divinely guaranteed purposes?
Relationship to Your View: Very close on responsibility under uncertainty

Author: John Dewey
Title: Human Nature and Conduct
Core Question / Why Read: How do moral practices emerge, evolve, and get tested in lived consequences?
Relationship to Your View: Close to constructed morality constrained by experience

Author: Christine M. Korsgaard
Title: The Sources of Normativity
Core Question / Why Read: Can constructed morality generate genuine obligations?
Relationship to Your View: Directly tests your tendency toward moral construction

Author: Albert Camus
Title: The Plague
Core Question / Why Read: What does responsibility look like when suffering has no guaranteed higher purpose?
Relationship to Your View: Very close to rejecting providential explanations of suffering

Author: Ibn Arabi
Title: The Bezels of Wisdom (Fusus al-Hikam)
Core Question / Why Read: How are God, Being, creation, and human perception related?
Relationship to Your View: Close metaphysically; major disagreement on prophetic privilege

Author: William C. Chittick
Title: The Sufi Path of Knowledge
Core Question / Why Read: What does it mean to know God, and what are the limits of such knowledge?
Relationship to Your View: Useful bridge into Ibn Arabi before primary texts

Author: William C. Chittick
Title: The Self-Disclosure of God
Core Question / Why Read: How does divine self-disclosure operate throughout existence?
Relationship to Your View: Close to your idea that all existence manifests Being

Author: Toshihiko Izutsu
Title: Sufism and Taoism
Core Question / Why Read: How do Ibn Arabi and Taoism conceptualize Being and ultimate Reality?
Relationship to Your View: Useful for separating metaphysics from exclusive religious identity

Author: William C. Chittick
Title: Divine Love: Islamic Literature and the Path to God
Core Question / Why Read: How does Islamic literature conceptualize divine love?
Relationship to Your View: Useful for understanding Islam sympathetically without assuming exclusivity

Author: Rumi
Title: The Masnavi (selected books)
Core Question / Why Read: Can spiritual insight exceed literal religious formulations?
Relationship to Your View: Close on experiential openness; retains Muhammad and revelation

Author: Farid ud-Din Attar
Title: The Conference of the Birds
Core Question / Why Read: What happens when the seeker confronts the self through the search for the divine?
Relationship to Your View: Strong literary complement to your view of literature as sacred manifestation

Author: Gregory A. Lipton
Title: Rethinking Ibn Arabi
Core Question / Why Read: How universalist was Ibn Arabi really?
Relationship to Your View: Important corrective against reading modern pluralism back into Ibn Arabi

Author: Abu Bakr al-Razi
Title: Study through scholarly secondary sources
Core Question / Why Read: If humans possess reason, why is privileged revelation necessary?
Relationship to Your View: One of the closest historical challenges to your prophecy objection; evidence is partly hostile/fragmentary

Author: Ibn al-Rawandi
Title: Study through scholarly secondary sources
Core Question / Why Read: What independent authority can revelation have over reason?
Relationship to Your View: Close to your skepticism; surviving evidence is fragmentary and often polemical

Author: Muhammad Iqbal
Title: The Reconstruction of Religious Thought in Islam
Core Question / Why Read: Can revelation coexist with intellectual independence and evolving human reason?
Relationship to Your View: Shares intellectual independence but retains Muhammad as prophet

Author: Pseudo-Dionysius
Title: The Mystical Theology
Core Question / Why Read: Can God be adequately described using human predicates at all?
Relationship to Your View: Very close to your anti-anthropomorphic caution

Author: Meister Eckhart
Title: Selected Writings
Core Question / Why Read: When do concepts of God become obstacles to ultimate reality?
Relationship to Your View: Close on limits of concepts; remains Christian

Author: Nicholas of Cusa
Title: On Learned Ignorance
Core Question / Why Read: What does it mean to know that finite minds cannot comprehend the infinite?
Relationship to Your View: Very close to your insistence on epistemic humility

Author: Ludwig Wittgenstein
Title: Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus
Core Question / Why Read: Where are the limits of meaningful language about reality?
Relationship to Your View: Useful pressure test for claims about God and Being

Author: William James
Title: The Varieties of Religious Experience
Core Question / Why Read: Can we take religious experience seriously without automatically accepting its theological interpretation?
Relationship to Your View: Extremely relevant to your distinction between experience and privileged interpretation

Author: Emmanuel Levinas
Title: Ethics and Infinity
Core Question / Why Read: Does responsibility arise in our encounter with another person rather than divine command?
Relationship to Your View: Strong complement to your human-responsibility principle; challenges ontology-first thinking

Author: T. M. Scanlon
Title: What We Owe to Each Other
Core Question / Why Read: Can morality rest on principles we can justify to one another?
Relationship to Your View: Strong secular framework for responsibility without revelation

Author: Jean-Paul Sartre
Title: Existentialism Is a Humanism
Core Question / Why Read: What follows if humans cannot outsource moral responsibility to a divine plan?
Relationship to Your View: Close on responsibility, though Sartre is atheistic

Author: Albert Camus
Title: The Rebel
Core Question / Why Read: How can we oppose injustice without invoking absolute divine authority?
Relationship to Your View: Close to your refusal to justify violence through transcendent claims

Author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
Title: The Brothers Karamazov
Core Question / Why Read: What do suffering, freedom, responsibility, and God mean together?
Relationship to Your View: A major challenge rather than simple agreement

Author: Jose Saramago
Title: The Gospel According to Jesus Christ
Core Question / Why Read: What happens when divine authority is examined from a radically human perspective?
Relationship to Your View: Directly relevant to authority and responsibility

Author: Hermann Hesse
Title: Siddhartha
Core Question / Why Read: Can spiritual understanding arise beyond inherited doctrine?
Relationship to Your View: Close to nonexclusive spiritual inquiry

Author: Ursula K. Le Guin
Title: The Dispossessed
Core Question / Why Read: How do constructed institutions shape freedom, obligation, and responsibility?
Relationship to Your View: Useful for testing constructed ethics socially

Author: Leo Tolstoy
Title: The Death of Ivan Ilyich
Core Question / Why Read: What makes a human life authentic or meaningful in the face of death?
Relationship to Your View: Useful non-scriptural encounter with Being and value

Author: Quran
Title: Selected surahs: 112, 2, 5, 49, 109
Core Question / Why Read: What does the Qur’an itself claim about divine unity, revelation, responsibility, human difference, and religious boundaries?
Relationship to Your View: Read as a primary text to test your interpretation rather than assuming either acceptance or rejection
